target_only_tests.note: Target-only seam-liveness tests, required by docs/test-translation-conventions.md rule 5. destination.ts and outbox.ts each route their uuid mint sites through a D-0014 seam record so a case needing a pinned id has a way to get one; interlock's own suite never needs it, so these have no source counterpart and are not counted as ported coverage. They exist because a seam nothing routes through is worse than no seam -- it looks like a control point while production goes around it.

entries.reason: ActionHandler.__subclasses__() has no JavaScript analogue. Two halves replace it, both asserted with anti-vacuity checks: a walk over the outbox/handlers/destination module namespaces (which, unlike __subclasses__, structurally excludes the handlers the cases below define, so the source's 'restricted to classes that actually ship' filter is free), and a source-text scan of those three files requiring every class that extends ActionHandler to be exported and therefore reachable by the walk. The declaration is an instance field in TypeScript where Python's is a class attribute, so each class is constructed to be asked.

inherited_limitations.topic: destination.py and handlers.py have no test file of their own anywhere in interlock.
inherited_limitations.detail: Both are specified entirely through tests/control_plane/test_outbox.py, which is why all three modules land in one change: separating them would put roughly 800 lines of production code in the tree with no specification at all. This is the source's structure, not a packaging choice made here, and it is the whole reason this PR exceeds the hand-written line cap.

inherited_limitations.topic: outbox.py declares its own EXACTLY_ONCE_MECHANISMS rather than importing lease's.
inherited_limitations.detail: The source duplicates the tuple in both modules and a ported case asserts the two copies are equal -- the value is ACCEPTANCE.md section 2's clause and the DDL's enumeration, not either module's policy. The port reproduces the duplication rather than collapsing it, so the case that guards against drift still has two things to compare.

inherited_limitations.topic: UNSUPPORTED_MECHANISMS is frozen where the source's is a plain dict.
inherited_limitations.detail: Lesson 13 says freeze what Python freezes; this freezes more. Harmless and unreachable from any ported case, but recorded rather than left as an undisclosed asymmetry.

inherited_limitations.topic: Outbox.load throws a bare Error where the source raises KeyError.
inherited_limitations.detail: Every bare ValueError in this module was given a dedicated OutboxUsageError, following the per-module convention; the KeyError path was not, so the class is less specific than the source's. No ported case asserts on it.

inherited_limitations.topic: Numeric reads follow D-0007's number mapping with no int()-style re-narrowing (D-0021).
inherited_limitations.detail: Unreachable through the public API under test.

inherited_limitations.topic: pythonRepr approximates Python's str.isprintable() rather than reproducing it.
inherited_limitations.detail: Python escapes any character isprintable() rejects. Reproducing that exactly needs the Unicode category table; the renderer escapes the classes reachable here -- C0, DEL, C1, the line and paragraph separators, and lone surrogates -- and emits other printable non-ASCII literally, as Python does. A character outside those classes that Python would nonetheless call unprintable would render literally here. Pinned by test/contract/python-repr.test.ts against values measured on CPython.

inherited_limitations.topic: A fenced write's no-op/stale classification is two statements, not one transaction.
inherited_limitations.detail: When _MARK_DELIVERED changes no row, the fence is re-read in a following statement to decide whether that was a benign duplicate or a superseded writer. A lease taken over between the two turns a legitimate deduplicated resend into a recorded StaleWriterRefused. interlock's _protected_write has the same two-step shape, so the port is at parity. Under the policy that replaced D-0022 this is to be repaired in continuo rather than disclosed indefinitely, but it is a concurrency redesign rather than a local fix, so it is scheduled into the control_plane repair belt with the other inherited defects rather than squeezed into this change. Raised by the Codex review gate (2026-08-22, P2).
